Solid game, playing 100% free to play you get like 50-100 hours of gameplay that's fun and engaging. It has the backbone of a solid mmo, good arpg soulslike combat system. Overall I'd give it a 8/10, the only reason it's not a 10/10 is because of how insane the cash shop pricing is for cosmetics. 200$ for a weapon, 2000$ to bling it out. It's just completely out of the price range of normal people to participate. I won't spend anything on the game until I see reasonably priced cosmetics, I understand the game needs funding but make the prices less then a monthly house mortgage maybe?

Just dive into it. If any advice, don't focus on those "collectibles" because they break an otherwise perfect immersion. To my own surprise, I went through the whole game in one playthrough, without a break. Couldn't take a break. It takes you to some very old and forgotten places, and some you hopefully don't know anything about (yet). The absence of UI, of character enhancement, of written tips makes you forget it's a game. You're just following (and often merging with) Senua. It was litterally breath taking, multiple times. But. This game is only for you if you're willing to dive in a unique experience rather than actually play a game, if you're willing to let yourself be Senua and not think you can just beat everything because, well, it's a game after all.

I can recommend this game. It is a good point-and-click type game. The hand-drawn graphics are gorgeous, the characters make you smile and the puzzles are nice and not too difficult.

To beat the game you need about an hour, for 100% you need about one and a half to two hours. A fair deal, considering the price of this game.

The game also has a great working Linux version. Nothing to complain about in this regard.

i've chewed on this for a year and ultimately i just don't love Silent Hill f as much as i want to. it's a perfectly competent horror game for the most part but i genuinely dislike the use of Higurashi style "you have to play through the game a bunch of times to not just get multiple endings, but to get any idea of what the ending is at all" in a game that is fairly lengthy and does not change enough on a second playthrough to stay fresh. i think all the dark world stuff is honestly pretty bad to play and the weird, fast-paced, combat-heavy gameplay is not good enough to be such a dominant focus of the game. it's a shame because i DO like the story and setting a lot, but as a game? i don't know. it just feels mediocre to play in a way i did not love.
More like a walking simulator with a few puzzles but a good walking sim with excellent visuals and audio. Rather short took just under 8 hours to do so I would get on sale

dredge is so magnificent. it is perfectly balanced between chill QTE and inventory management and harrowing near misses. the gameplay never feels monotonous which, for a fishing game, is saying something. it throws a lot of side quests and mysteries at you right off the bat to get you hooked (heh) but there is also no time limit on any of them which means you can spend all your time grinding and getting your bag if you want to (i mean, peacefully fishing on beautiful blue waves...). the score is beautiful and evokes the nostalgic, somewhat melancholy sounds of ghibli films. this game is a 8.5/10 for me. i wish the NPCs had just a little more depth, but that isn't to say that they're shallow because they absolutely are not. i'm only 5 hours in, but i already love this game.

I agree with those who say wait for a good sale and it's very short, even though I got it at 30% off it's not nearly enough. The game is not bad (it's like Contra or Megaman for fair comparison) but it is very short (30-35 minutes) and I am not a pixel graphics fan either. There are some additional gameplay modes to unlock but that doesn't add a ton of time and it doesn't take much effort. You can easily play through it, get most of the achievements in less than 2 hours and refund.
Wait for at least a 75% sale to pick this one up. Even at just under $20 with bundle savings it's still way overpriced for how short it is.

A short game masterfully crafted by ISART students (Out of Seats Studio). It features a beautiful art style, a great atmosphere, enjoyable gameplay, and excellent engine optimization.
I even increased the ResolutionQuality value in the GameUserSettings.ini on purpose, and the game still showed no major frame rate drops. That is a clear sign of solid optimization, which has become quite rare these days. It's especially worth highlighting because the game runs so well without relying on DLSS or FSR. On top of that, it supports native ultrawide out of the box!
Truly impressive work! Congratulations to the entire team! I can't wait to see what you create next.

STORY 
 “The hero will sacrifice you to save the world, while the villain will sacrifice the world to save you.” 
And only when you reach the end of the game will you understand which one you are.

 ATMOSPHERE 
A game reminiscent of Little Nightmares, but played from a first-person perspective, featuring puzzles involving fire and the ability to change locations by listening carefully and closing your eyes.

 GAMEPLAY EXPERIENCE 
The gameplay is interesting, but the game has its fair share of bugs. I wouldn’t recommend exploring every corner of the map, as you’ll get stuck in the geometry, forcing you to lose progress and restart from a checkpoint. It’s incredibly frustrating.
Only when I started playing more linearly, without unnecessary exploration, did I truly begin to enjoy the game.
